title: Module 10 · Trauma
intro: TXA timing, massive transfusion and calcium, RSI in shock, anticoagulated falls, TBI osmotherapy and seizure prophylaxis, open fractures, tetanus, VTE prophylaxis and pain, burns and a trauma night.

cases.title: TXA in the trauma bay
cases.stem: Motorcycle crash. Injury time 1:40 ago. HR 128, SBP 84. EMS gave nothing.

options.t: 1 g IV over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 hours
1 g IV over 10 min, then 1 g over 24 hours
options.why: The second gram runs over 8 hours.

options.t: 1 g IV over 10 min only, no infusion
options.why: Missing the 8 hour infusion (except some prehospital bolus protocols).

options.t: 10 mg/kg IV, then 1 mg/kg/h for 24 hours

steps.q: What is the time limit and why?

options.t: Within 3 hours of injury; later may harm
options.why: CRASH-2: benefit greatest early; harm after 3 hours.
The clock starts at injury, not arrival.
Bleeding deaths rose when started after 3 hours.

steps.q: What do you ask EMS first?

options.t: Injury time and any TXA given
options.why: Prevents a late start or a duplicate dose.

cases.pearl: **TXA: 1 g over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h, only within 3 hours. Ask EMS.**

sources.t: CRASH-2 collaborators. Tranexamic acid in trauma patients with significant haemorrhage. Lancet 2010;376:23-32

cases.title: Massive transfusion and calcium
cases.stem: Ten units of blood products so far. Ionized calcium 0.82 mmol/L. BP still low.

options.t: Citrate in stored blood binds calcium

options.why: Ionized calcium is already corrected for albumin.

options.t: CaCl 1 g IV (central) or gluconate 3 g IV
Calcium gluconate 1 g IV once only
options.why: One third of the calcium in 1 g chloride; usually too little.

options.t: Wait until transfusion ends to treat
options.why: Low calcium worsens bleeding and shock now.

steps.q: What ratio of products do trauma programs aim for?

options.why: PROPPR arm with no mortality benefit at 24 h and 30 d.

options.t: Red cells only until labs return

options.why: Large crystalloid volumes worsen trauma outcomes.

cases.pearl: **Massive transfusion: 1:1:1, and replace calcium (CaCl 1 g or Ca gluconate 3 g).**

sources.t: Holcomb JB, et al. 1:1:1 vs 1:1:2 transfusion ratio (PROPPR). JAMA 2015;313:471-482

cases.title: Intubating a trauma patient in shock

options.why: Drops blood pressure; at most a much reduced dose.

steps.q: Which paralytic, and how long does it last?

options.t: Rocuronium 1 to 1.2 mg/kg; lasts 45 to 60 min

options.why: 0.6 mg/kg is the non RSI dose; it lasts about 30 to 40 minutes.

options.t: Succinylcholine 1.5 mg/kg in a 3 day old crush
options.why: Hyperkalemia risk after 48 to 72 hours in crush and burns.
A priming dose; not an RSI dose.

steps.q: What must start right after the tube is in?

options.t: Analgesia and sedation, as BP allows
options.why: Rocuronium outlasts the induction drug: awake paralysis risk.

cases.pearl: **Shock RSI: ketamine or etomidate + rocuronium, then analgesia and sedation right away.**

sources.t: St. Mary's trauma activation, massive transfusion, TXA and open fracture protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: Ketamine 1 to 2 mg/kg x 85 = 85 to 170 mg; etomidate 0.3 x 85 = 25.5 mg; rocuronium 1 to 1.2 x 85 = 85 to 102 mg.

cases.title: Anticoagulated fall
cases.stem: An 84 year old fell and hit her head. CT shows a subdural hematoma. Med list says "blood thinner."

options.t: Identify the anticoagulant and last dose time
Give vitamin K 10 mg IV to every patient
Order an anti Xa level and wait

steps.q: She takes rivaroxaban, last dose 4 hours ago. Reversal?

options.why: Often 50 units/kg or a fixed dose; andexanet withdrawn from the US in 2025.

cases.title: Severe TBI: osmotherapy
cases.stem: Severe TBI with signs of herniation. Weight 80 kg. Central line in place.

options.t: Mannitol 0.25 to 1 g/kg IV (20 to 80 g)
3% saline 250 mL, or 23.4% 30 mL central only

options.why: CRASH: steroids increased death in TBI.

options.t: 23.4% saline 30 mL through a peripheral IV

options.why: Brain Trauma Foundation 4th edition: phenytoin; levetiracetam widely used.
Prophylaxis does not prevent late seizures.

options.t: For life after any severe TBI
CRASH-3: helps mild to moderate TBI within 3 h
CRASH-3: helps severe TBI at any time
options.why: No clear benefit in severe TBI.

options.t: CRASH-3: helps all TBI within 8 hours
CRASH-3: TXA raised seizures and deaths
options.why: No increase in vascular events or seizures.

cases.pearl: **TBI: mannitol or hypertonic saline (23.4% central only), seizure prophylaxis 7 days, no steroids.**

sources.t: Carney N, et al. Brain Trauma Foundation guidelines for severe TBI, 4th edition. Neurosurgery 2017;80:6-15
CRASH-3 collaborators. Tranexamic acid in traumatic brain injury. Lancet 2019;394:1713-1723
St. Mary's trauma activation, massive transfusion, TXA and open fracture protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: Mannitol 0.25 to 1 g/kg x 80 = 20 to 80 g (20% = 100 to 400 mL).

cases.title: Open fracture antibiotics
cases.stem: Open tibia fracture with a large wound and soil contamination (type III). 130 kg.

options.why: Not first line; weight based if used.

options.t: Add gram negative coverage per protocol
Add vancomycin for every type III
Add metronidazole for every type III

cases.pearl: **Open fracture: cefazolin within 1 hour (3 g if 120 kg+). Type III: add gram negative.**

sources.t: EAST practice management guideline: open fracture antibiotics (2022) and trauma VTE prophylaxis (via St. Mary's wiki Trauma page)

cases.title: Tetanus
cases.stem: A deep wound contaminated with soil. The patient is not sure he ever had tetanus shots.

options.why: Unknown history and a dirty wound.
A treatment dose for clinical tetanus.

options.t: Tetanus immune globulin in the same syringe as Tdap

steps.q: Clean minor wound, fully vaccinated, last dose 7 years ago. Vaccine?

options.t: No; booster only if over 10 years for clean wounds
Yes; booster if over 5 years for any wound

options.why: TIG only for unknown or fewer than 3 doses with dirty wounds.

options.t: Yes; every ER visit needs a booster

cases.pearl: **Clean wound: booster if over 10 years. Dirty: over 5 years. Unknown or fewer than 3 doses + dirty: add TIG 250 units.**

sources.t: CDC: clinical guidance for wound management to prevent tetanus

cases.title: Trauma VTE prophylaxis and pain
cases.stem: Day 2 after pelvic fractures, bleeding stable, 90 kg, CrCl 100. Rib fractures too.

options.t: Enoxaparin per protocol once bleeding allows
options.why: Often 30 mg q12h or 40 mg daily, adjusted by weight and anti Xa.

options.t: Warfarin to INR 2 to 3, starting today
options.why: Slow, hard to reverse; not trauma prophylaxis.
NSAIDs if safe; opioids as needed.

cases.pearl: **Trauma: enoxaparin early when safe. Ribs: multimodal pain control.**

sources.t: EAST practice management guideline: open fracture antibiotics (2022) and trauma VTE prophylaxis (via St. Mary's wiki Trauma page)

cases.title: Burns: Parkland formula
cases.stem: 80 kg, 40% total body surface area burn, burn time 2 hours ago.

options.why: Parkland; ABA now suggests starting at 2 to 4 mL/kg/%TBSA.

options.t: 2 x 80 x 40 = 6,400 mL LR in 24 h
options.why: The lower ABA start; Parkland uses 4.

options.t: 4 x 80 x 40 = 1,280 mL LR in 24 h
4 x 80 x 40 = 12,800 mL NS in 8 h

steps.q: How much in the first 8 hours, and from when?

options.why: Half by hour 8 after the burn; 2 hours have passed.
Half of the total goes in the first 8 hours from the burn.

cases.pearl: **Parkland: 4 x kg x %TBSA. Half in 8 hours from the burn time.**

sources.t: St. Mary's trauma activation, massive transfusion, TXA and open fracture protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: 4 x 80 x 40 = **12,800 mL**; half = 6,400 mL by hour 8 from the burn; 2 hours gone, so 6,400 mL over 6 hours = **1,067 mL/h**, then 6,400 mL over 16 hours = 400 mL/h.

cases.title: Shift simulation: trauma night
cases.stem: Three items: (1) a hypotensive GSW patient arriving now, injury 25 minutes ago; (2) an open fracture patient whose cefazolin is 40 minutes late; (3) a CIWA question on the trauma floor.

steps.q: For the alcohol withdrawal patient, what must come before glucose?

options.why: Given, but not the step before glucose.

cases.pearl: **Bleeding first, late antibiotics second, withdrawal questions third. Thiamine before glucose.**
